about: Suggested starting points for a rock cover band, offered in the My tone dialog. Each is added only when the player presses Add.

tweaks.text: Band mix with a bass player: the bass and kick own the low end. Low cut 110-120 Hz on every tone (130-150 Hz on high-gain rhythm), on the cab or a post-amp EQ, and high cut around 7-8 kHz (6-6.5 kHz on high gain) to take off fizz.

Cut the mud on every tone, every guitar and every rig: a Parametric EQ cut of 4-5 dB at 420 Hz (Q about 1), right after the amp and cab. With a full-rig NAM capture (cab included) it goes right after the capture.

Mid scoops are welcome: on high-gain amps, especially the Cali Rectifire and other Mesa-style amps, scoop the mids (amp Mid 2-4) for a tight, heavy rhythm tone. Use the solo snapshot's boost, not more treble, when a lead needs to cut through.
Use about 20-30% less amp gain than sounds best on its own: in a band, too much gain turns to mush. Get extra sustain from a low-gain, high-level drive in front instead.

Keep ambience tighter than the record: reverb Mix 10-20%, delay Mix 15-25%, switched on for leads and off for rhythm. Low cut reverb and delay at 150-200 Hz and high cut them at 5-6 kHz so they add space, not mud or hiss.
Level-match the snapshots: rhythm sections at the same loudness, and the solo or lead snapshot 2-3 dB louder by switching on a boost or drive whose Level sits that much hot, never more than 4 dB.
Assume a mono PA: nothing that relies on hard-panned ping-pong or wide stereo, and no effect that cancels or vanishes when summed to mono.
Single coils: tame the bridge pickup's ice-pick with Treble or Presence 0.5-1 lower and a high cut near 6.5 kHz on driven tones.
Humbuckers: low cut at the top of the range (120 Hz, 150 Hz on high gain) on top of the 420 Hz cut, and about 10% less gain on neck-pickup leads.

gear_notes.name: Parametric
gear_notes.text: My default band EQ, right after the amp/cab (or a full-rig NAM capture): Low Cut 110-120 Hz (130-150 Hz on high gain), 420 Hz at -4 to -5 dB with Q about 1, High Cut 7-8 kHz. Leave the other bands flat unless the song needs them.

gear_notes.name: Scream 808
gear_notes.text: In front of a high-gain amp it's a tightener: Gain 0-2, Tone 5-6, Level 7-8. In front of a clean or crunch amp it's a mid-hump solo boost.

gear_notes.name: Minotaur
gear_notes.text: Transparent solo boost: Gain 2-3, Treble at noon, Output for about +3 dB, switched on in the lead snapshot.

gear_notes.name: Cali Rectifire
gear_notes.text: Scoop the mids: Mid 2-4, Bass moderate (4-5) and tighten the lows with the low cut instead, Presence to taste. Pair with the Parametric's 420 Hz cut and a Scream 808 tightener in front for rhythm.

gear_notes.name: Reverb
gear_notes.text: Low cut 150-200 Hz, high cut 5-6 kHz, Mix 10-20% in the band (more only for a part that's clearly ambient). Keep it last, after the delay.

gear_notes.name: Delay
gear_notes.text: Synced to the song's tempo, trails on, high cut 4-6 kHz so repeats sit behind the guitar. Mix 15-25% on leads, about 10% on rhythm.

gear_notes.name: Distortion
gear_notes.text: Into an amp that's already crunchy, use it as a boost (low Gain, high Level), not as more distortion. Don't stack two high-gain drives.

gear_notes.name: Dynamics
gear_notes.text: Compressors stay light (2-4 dB of gain reduction) for cleans, funk and arpeggios, and off on high gain. Gates sit just above the hiss so they don't chop note tails.

gear_notes.name: Modulation
gear_notes.text: Mix lower than sounds good alone (under about 40%) and mono-safe; chorus mostly on cleans.

gear_notes.name: Dual Rectifier
gear_notes.text: Scoop the mids and tighten it: Parametric after it with -5 dB at 420 Hz, low cut 130-150 Hz, high cut 6.5 kHz; Scream 808 in front as a tightener and a Noise Gate before the drives.

gear_notes.name: 6505 Lead
gear_notes.text: Scream 808 tightener in front, Noise Gate, then a Parametric after it: low cut 130-150 Hz, -5 dB at 420 Hz, high cut 6 kHz for the fizz. Mid scoops suit it.

gear_notes.name: JCM800
gear_notes.text: The top end can fizz: high cut about 6.5 kHz on top of the usual -4 to -5 dB at 420 Hz. Push solos with the Minotaur rather than more gain.

gear_notes.name: Plexi
gear_notes.text: With humbuckers it gets woolly: low cut 120 Hz with the usual 420 Hz cut. With a Strat bridge pickup, high cut about 7 kHz too.

gear_notes.name: Twin Reverb
gear_notes.text: Clean platform: the usual low cut and 420 Hz cut still apply; a light compressor (Deluxe Comp) for funk or strummed parts.

gear_notes.name: AC30 Greenback
gear_notes.text: Chime can turn harsh at volume: if it's too bright, cut 2 dB around 3 kHz rather than rolling off the whole top.
